We ruined your mood and broke your radio.

Nina, do you know what I thought?
It's time for me to get smart. Seriously.

words.gloss: to take hold, to get down to
words.gram: infinitive, imperfective (браться за ум = get smart)

браться.gloss: to take hold of, to get down to

meanings.en: to set about, to undertake, to take hold of
meanings.note: браться за ум = to get smart, to come to one's senses

examples.trans: It's time for me to get smart.
He eagerly gets down to work.

examples.text: Мне за ум пора браться. Серьёзно.
examples.trans: It's time for me to get smart. Seriously.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?
I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.en: after all, still, all the same
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'ё-таки').

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: после вчерашнего = after what happened yesterday

examples.text: Ты что здесь делаешь? После вчерашнего!
examples.trans: What are you doing here? After yesterday!

examples.text: А то ты вчерашний вечер не помнишь?
examples.trans: As if you don't remember last night?

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you
after 2, 3, 4: года; after 5 and more: лет

examples.trans: I've been working here for four years.

examples.text: Это было давно, тридцать лет назад.
examples.trans: That was long ago, thirty years back.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: жить в гостинице = to stay at a hotel

examples.text: Ладно, поезжай в гостиницу, ты устала.
examples.trans: Alright, go to the hotel, you're tired.
We stayed at a small hotel.

examples.text: Ладно, поезжай в гостиницу, ты устала. Спасибо!
examples.trans: Alright, go to the hotel, you're tired. Thank you!

давно.gloss: for a long time; long ago

meanings.note: with present: Я давно здесь = I've been here a long time

examples.trans: You haven't been interested in me for a long time.

examples.text: Вспомнил? Я давно тебя не интересую.
examples.trans: Now you remember? You haven't been interested in me for a long time.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

испортить.gloss: to ruin, to spoil, to break

meanings.note: испортить настроение = to ruin someone's mood

examples.text: А я испорчу отношения с будущим мэром.
examples.trans: And I'll ruin my relationship with the future mayor.
She is reading a children's book.

examples.text: Надо пить меньше. Книжки буду читать.
examples.trans: I need to drink less. I'm going to read books.
All right, here you go. There, look.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! А ты заикаешься меньше.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! And you stutter less.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'строение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'mood, spirits' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вот с таким настроением и иди к Аникееву.
examples.trans: Go to Anikeev in just that mood.
I am in a good mood today.

examples.text: С таким настроением, конечно, не будет.
examples.trans: With an attitude like that, of course there won't be.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I have no money at all.

examples.text: Да нет у тебя никаких денег.
examples.trans: But you don't have any money.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

meanings.note: used on its own: он пьёт = he drinks

examples.text: Всё, теперь ты герой? И можно только пить?
examples.trans: So now you're a hero? And all you have to do is drink?

related.gloss: to go on a drinking binge

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'держка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'support, backing' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There you go! No support at all!
I really need the family's support.

meanings.en: to think it over, to give it a thought

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

поехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to set off

meanings.en: to go, to set off (by car, bus, train)

examples.trans: All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.

meanings.note: as a conjunction: пока я сплю
+ infinitive: Пора идти = Time to go

examples.trans: It's time for us to go.
All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

examples.text: Мы тебе настроение испортили и приёмник сломали.
examples.trans: We ruined your mood and broke your radio.
An old radio stood on the table.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'фессионал'). Common masculine noun meaning 'professional' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У вас тут в провинции одни профессионалы.
examples.trans: You've got nothing but professionals out here in the provinces.

examples.text: Ты настоящий профессионал! Ты знаешь психологию.
examples.trans: You're a real professional! You know psychology.

meanings.en: to grow, to grow up, to develop
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to grow, to grow up', paired with 'вырасти'.

examples.text: Вообще надо расти во всех смыслах.
examples.trans: In general, I need to grow in every sense.
The road here is smooth and wide.

examples.text: И стыки у тебя ровные! Пока, Даня!
examples.trans: And your joints are even! Bye, Danya!

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: сломать руку = to break one's arm

examples.text: Меня жена бросила. Два пальца сломаны.
examples.trans: My wife has left me. Two of my fingers are broken.
What do you mean? Where is Mishkin?

meanings.note: + genitive plural: сорок рублей; other cases: сорока

examples.trans: I don't know. Forty, I think.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: where two pipes or rails meet

examples.trans: The craftsman checked all the pipe joints.

examples.text: А стыки, Даня, у тебя всё равно неровные!
examples.trans: And your seams, Danya, are still uneven!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: 1st person singular future is not used by itself

examples.text: Ты его убедила? Ты уверена в этом?
examples.trans: You convinced him? Are you sure about this?

examples.text: Что-то голос какой-то не очень уверенный.
examples.trans: Your voice doesn't sound very confident.
He answered in a calm, confident voice.

examples.text: Что-то голос какой-то не очень уверенный. Что конкретно?
examples.trans: Your voice doesn't sound very confident. What specifically?

удивиться.gloss: to be surprised, to be amazed

examples.trans: Just wait and see, you'll be surprised yet!
I was very surprised by his words.

examples.text: Я сам удивился, когда ощипывал его.
examples.trans: I was surprised myself when I was plucking it.

meanings.note: сойти с ума = to go mad, lose one's mind

examples.text: Позвонить Третьякову? Я что, с ума сошёл?
examples.trans: Call Tretyakov? What, have I lost my mind?

meanings.en: to get tired, to grow weary
meanings.note: past tense устал / устала often means 'am/is tired'

examples.trans: I am very tired of sitting.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to read', paired with 'прочитать'.

examples.trans: What are you reading right now?
You don't read the small print.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
